title: Elastic and inelastic collisions
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:41Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points covers kinetic energy in elastic and inelastic collisions; the economics elasticity points are unrelated, and the Units 1 and 2 momentum and impulse point covers momentum conservation but not the energy difference between collision types.

draft.title: Elastic and inelastic collisions
card: In every collision in an isolated system, total momentum is conserved. This is true whether or not kinetic energy is kept.
total kinetic energy is the same before and after the collision. The objects bounce apart with no energy turned into other forms.
some kinetic energy is lost from the motion. It becomes other forms, such as heat, sound or the energy of deforming the objects.
To classify a collision, compare total kinetic energy (½mv² for each object, added up) before and after. Equal means elastic. Less after means inelastic.
draft.remember: Momentum is conserved in both types. Only an elastic collision keeps all the kinetic energy.

a.q: Two trolleys collide and stick together. Total momentum is the same before and after, but kinetic energy falls. What kind of collision is this?
opts: Inelastic, because kinetic energy was lost
Elastic, because the trolleys moved together
Inelastic, because momentum was not conserved
a.why: Kinetic energy fell, so the collision is inelastic. Momentum is conserved in both types, so conserved momentum cannot show that a collision is elastic.
a.clue: Which quantity tells the two types apart?

b.q: A 2.0 kg trolley moving at 3.0 m/s hits a stationary 1.0 kg trolley. Afterwards they move apart at 1.0 m/s and 4.0 m/s respectively. What type of collision is this?
opts: Elastic, as kinetic energy stays at 9.0 J
Inelastic, as kinetic energy falls from 9.0 J
Inelastic, as momentum falls from 6.0 kg m/s
Elastic, as the trolleys move apart afterwards
b.why: Before: ½ × 2.0 × 3.0² = 9.0 J. After: ½ × 2.0 × 1.0² + ½ × 1.0 × 4.0² = 1.0 + 8.0 = 9.0 J. Kinetic energy is kept, so it is elastic. Momentum is 6.0 kg m/s before and after (2.0 + 4.0), so it is conserved.
b.clue: Add up the kinetic energy of both trolleys before and after.

a.best: Inelastic, because kinetic energy was lost

b.best: Elastic, as kinetic energy stays at 9.0 J

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions check out: in (b), momentum is 6.0 kg m/s and kinetic energy is 9.0 J both before and after, so the collision is elastic as intended.
